record.paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
record.context_brief: Centers of distances of adjoint Cantorvals
record.original_question: For q in (0, 1/2), compute the center of distances of the adjoint Cantorval associated with the geometric central Cantor set E(q^n).

evidence.quote: Given a central Cantor set C = C(an), the union Gn of all intervals removed at the n-th step is well-defined. Define Cb := C ∪ ⋃_{n∈2N−1} Gn, which is a Cantorval called the adjoint Cantorval of C.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a nonempty subset $A$ of a metric space $(X,d)$, define the center of distances of $A$ by
$$S(A):=\{\alpha\in[0,\infty): \forall x\in A\ \exists y\in A\ \ d(x,y)=\alpha\}.$$

Given a sequence $(a_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of positive reals with $a_n\le \tfrac{1}{2}(a_{n-1}+\cdots)$ (so that the construction below produces a Cantor-type set in $[0,1]$), the central Cantor set $C=C(a_n)$ is constructed as follows. Start with $I_0=[0,1]$. At step $n\ge 1$, from each of the $2^{n-1}$ closed intervals of length $\ell_{n-1}$ obtained at the previous step, remove an open middle interval so that each remaining interval has length $a_n$; this yields $2^n$ closed intervals of length $a_n$ and an additional collection of $2^{n-1}$ open "gap" intervals removed at step $n$, whose union is denoted $G_n$. Then $C=\bigcap_{n\ge 0} I_n$, where $I_n$ is the union of the $2^n$ closed intervals at step $n$.

The adjoint Cantorval of $C$ is defined as
$$\widehat C := C\ \cup\ \bigcup_{n\in 2\mathbb{N}-1} G_n,$$
i.e., $C$ together with all gaps removed at odd-numbered steps.

For $q\in(0,\tfrac12)$ let $E(q^n)$ denote the geometric central Cantor set obtained by taking $a_n=q^n$ in the construction above (so the surviving intervals at step $n$ have length $q^n$). 

Determine explicitly the center of distances $S(\widehat{E(q^n)})$ of the adjoint Cantorval of $E(q^n)$, as a function of $q\in(0,\tfrac12)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2022–2025) develops the center-of-distances theory for central Cantor sets and Cantorvals (e.g., Banakiewicz–Bartoszewicz–Filipczak; Bielas–Plewik), but no published computation of the center of distances of the adjoint Cantorval of the geometric central Cantor set $E(q^n)$ for $q\in(0,1/2)$ was located. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Center of Distances of Central Cantor Sets
status_evidence.snippet: Studies S(C) for central Cantor sets C(a_n) but does not address adjoint Cantorvals of geometric E(q^n).
status_evidence.claim: Center of distances has been computed for central Cantor sets, but the adjoint-Cantorval case for geometric q^n is not resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Center of Distances and Central Cantor Sets
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces and develops the notion S(A) for central Cantor sets.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational paper on centers of distances; does not contain the adjoint-Cantorval geometric computation.

status_evidence.title: On generating regular Cantorvals connected with geometric Cantor sets
status_evidence.snippet: Studies geometric Cantor sets E(q^n) and associated Cantorvals.
status_evidence.claim: Discusses adjoint/regular Cantorvals from geometric Cantor sets without computing their centers of distances.
